subject: Setting the range and defining basis functions for B.tau and B.kappa

messages.author: 8e91233dacfe731a
messages.subject: Setting the range and defining basis functions for B.tau and B.kappa
parts:
Hi folks,

Are there some general guidelines for setting the spatial range of an SPDE model when dealing with a large geographical domain, islands within the mesh and large areas with no observations (see code and data attached)? The example provided in section 2.3 of Lindgren & Rue (2013) has been most helpful in understanding the relationships between the range, kappa, tau and sigma. However, I'd like to alter the default specification of the 'inla.spde2.matern' function to see how modifying the B.tau and B.kappa matrices influences the spatial random effect in a stationary model, but am a little unsure as how best to define "range0".

On a related note (and apologies if this has been covered elsewhere), what effect, in general, does altering the basis functions in columns 2 and 3 of B.tau and B.kappa have on the behaviour of the spatial random effect?

Any info on these points would be greatly appreciated!

Thanks,
Jed

messages.author: 8e91233dacfe731a
messages.subject: Re: Setting the range and defining basis functions for B.tau and B.kappa
parts:
Just an additional point here. The original question in the previous post was motivated by the observation that the addition of the the spatial effect, as defined through the default specification of the inla.spde2.matern function, often seemed to 'swamp' the covariate effects in situations where you would expect the covariates to have a stronger influence on the response even after spatial autocorrelation is accounted for.

Best,
Jed
